timeline.title: Chicago Whip founded
timeline.description: Black weekly newspaper founded; circulation 65,000 within a year; later no documented archive.

timeline.title: Tulsa Race Massacre
timeline.description: Destruction of Greenwood - the canonical origin event for Black memory erasure.

timeline.title: Schomburg collection founded
timeline.description: Arturo Schomburg's personal collection becomes the research library that would become the Schomburg Center.

timeline.title: Vivian Harsh starts "Special Negro Collection"
timeline.description: Unfunded weekly "Book Hour" and collection at Hall Branch; becomes the Harsh Research Collection.

timeline.title: Vee-Jay Records founded
timeline.description: First Black-owned, female-founded major indie label (Gary, Indiana).

timeline.title: Emmett Till murdered; Roberts Temple funeral
timeline.description: Till funeral at Roberts Temple Church of God in Christ, Chicago; open-casket photograph changes history. A.A. Rayner & Sons provided funeral services.
timeline.source: NPS; A.A. Rayner & Sons firm site

timeline.title: Muhammad Speaks founded
timeline.description: Nation of Islam paper becomes the largest-circulating Black newspaper of its day; its own archive location undocumented.

timeline.title: WVON launched as Black-oriented talk station
timeline.description: WVON becomes the Voice of the Nation; its 1960s broadcast record survives almost entirely through private collectors' airchecks.

timeline.title: Lucky Cordell / Ed Cook WVON airchecks recorded
timeline.description: Home recordings of WVON broadcasts - now the surviving record of the era.

timeline.title: FBI/police raids seize Black Panther Party records
timeline.description: Raids in Denver, Indianapolis, Des Moines, San Francisco, New Bedford, Toledo, New Orleans, Detroit seize "file cabinets, party records"; no centralized Panther archive exists.

timeline.title: DJ Screw born (Robert Earl Davis Jr.)
timeline.description: Originator of chopped-and-screwed music; personal archive later becomes the UH Libraries DJ Screw Collection.

timeline.title: Ovie Carter wins Pulitzer
timeline.description: Chicago Tribune photographer (1969-2004); personal negative archive disposition undocumented.

timeline.title: Center for Black Music Research founded
timeline.description: CBMR founded at Columbia College Chicago; library/archives 1990.

timeline.title: Amistad Research Center moves to Tulane
timeline.description: Amistad (founded 1966 at Fisk; independent 1969) relocates to Tulane University.

timeline.title: Eyes on the Prize rights blackout
timeline.description: The rights-driven withdrawal of the civil-rights documentary series (ca. 1995) and its return (2005-2006) - a decade-long rights blackout of a landmark series.

timeline.title: WDCU license sale
timeline.description: Howard University sells jazz station license - warning case of ownership change endangering Black cultural assets.

timeline.title: Teenie Harris dies; archive acquired by Carnegie Museum of Art
timeline.description: Harris dies June 12, 1998; Carnegie Museum of Art acquires ~80,000 negatives from the family in 2001; decades-long public-identification program begins.

timeline.title: The HistoryMakers founded
timeline.description: Julieanna Richardson founds The HistoryMakers in Chicago.

timeline.title: DJ Screw dies
timeline.description: Robert Earl Davis Jr. dies; family will steward his tapes until the 2011 UH donation.

timeline.title: The Baltimore Collection donated to University of Delaware
timeline.description: 53 photographs of Black sitters arrive as "found objects" - no provenance.

timeline.title: Partners for Sacred Places lists Pilgrim Baptist as a site to save
timeline.description: "Ten Sacred Places to Save" (2001): Pilgrim Baptist's leaking roof needed $2.8M; fire would follow in 2006.

timeline.title: NMAAHC established by Congress
timeline.description: National Museum of African American History and Culture established by Act of Congress.

timeline.title: Hurricane Katrina floods Calhoun-McCormick archive
timeline.description: Keith Calhoun and Chandra McCormick evacuate New Orleans with ~30 years of film in bins; return to waterlogged negatives.

timeline.title: Pilgrim Baptist Church fire
timeline.description: Fire guts Pilgrim Baptist, birthplace of Black gospel music, destroying its music and records archive.

timeline.title: BlackPast.org founded
timeline.description: Quintard Taylor founds the digital encyclopedia of Black history.

timeline.title: America's Black Holocaust Museum closes
timeline.description: Museum closes; virtual museum launches 2012.

timeline.title: Universal Studios vault fire destroys Chess masters
timeline.description: UMG warehouse fire destroys master recordings including Chess; exact title losses contested.

timeline.title: 2009-2011 BMRC survey documents underprocessing
timeline.description: BMRC survey finds Chicago's Black collections systematically unprocessed/underprocessed.

timeline.title: Moorland-Spingarn closure scare
timeline.description: Reports of MSRC's ~80% staff reduction; director Thomas C. Battle on record.

timeline.title: Google News Archive homepage removed
timeline.description: First major platform-level disappearance of newspaper-digitization access.

timeline.title: DJ Screw Collection donation begins at UH
timeline.description: Family donates DJ Screw's papers, 1,600+ records, original screw tapes to UH Libraries (finding aid 2010-023).

timeline.title: Black Archives Co begins
timeline.description: Renata Cherlise starts Black Archives Co on Tumblr - 13+ year crowdsourced archive of Black-life photographs.

timeline.title: CBMR defunding threat
timeline.description: Columbia College prioritization proposes eliminating CBMR funding after ~70% budget cuts since 2006.
timeline.source: Journal of Blacks in Higher Education, 2012

timeline.title: Gates acquires Stony Island bank building
timeline.description: Theaster Gates purchases the 1923 bank (vacant since the 1980s, slated for demolition) from the city for $1.

timeline.title: Mother Bethel records moved to Presbyterian Historical Society
timeline.description: Mother Bethel AME's archives (founded 1794) outgrow church storage; moved to PHS.

timeline.title: Library of Congress acquires The HistoryMakers
timeline.description: LoC acquires the ~3,400-interview video oral history archive.
timeline.source: Journal of Blacks in Higher Education, 2014

timeline.title: Freedmen's Bureau Project launches
timeline.description: 19,000+ volunteers index 4M records in ~18 months.

timeline.title: Stony Island Arts Bank opens
timeline.description: Rebuild Foundation opens the Arts Bank with the JPC library, Frankie Knuckles vinyl, Edward J. Williams Collection, and 60,000+ UChicago lantern slides.

timeline.title: NMAAHC opens to the public
timeline.description: Museum opens with 37,000-45,000 objects; 10,000+ digitized.

timeline.title: Vine shuts down
timeline.description: Vine shutdown and the cultural erasure of Black digital creative expression.

timeline.title: John Hope Franklin estate sale
timeline.description: Sale of the eminent scholar's personal library and archives - warning case.

timeline.title: Obsidian Collection Archives founded
timeline.description: Angela Ford founds Obsidian (Chicago) to digitize Black press photography.

timeline.title: LOC Twitter archive goes selective
timeline.description: End of comprehensive platform-scale tweet capture.

timeline.title: Tumblr adult-content purge
timeline.description: Platform purge and collateral data loss for Black digital archives on Tumblr.

timeline.title: MySpace server-migration loss disclosed
timeline.description: All user uploads 2003-2015 lost: ~50M songs from ~14M artists.

timeline.title: Johnson Publishing Company files Chapter 7
timeline.description: Bankruptcy begins; Ebony/Jet archive faces auction.

timeline.title: JPC archive auction; consortium purchase
timeline.description: Four-foundation consortium buys the archive for just under $30M, forestalling private dispersal.

timeline.title: Roberts Temple named to National Trust 11 Most Endangered
timeline.description: Emmett Till funeral site listed among America's 11 Most Endangered Historic Places.

timeline.title: #BlackLivesMatter tweets decay (Pew study, 2023)
timeline.description: Pew finds 18% of 2020-2022 #BLM tweets deleted or unavailable - first quantified decay rate for a Black movement's digital record.

timeline.title: Separate Cinema archive exhibited (PBS SoCal)
timeline.description: Kisch's 37,000-item race-film memorabilia collection profiled before its 2025 museum acquisition.

timeline.title: Mother Bethel digitization completed
timeline.description: Presbyterian Historical Society completes digitization of Mother Bethel AME records.

timeline.title: BMRC Archives Portal launches
timeline.description: Public portal aggregating 1,000+ Chicago Black-history collection records (Mellon-funded).

timeline.title: JPC archive transfers to NMAAHC/Getty
timeline.description: Joint ownership; $30M Getty commitment to processing and digitization.

timeline.title: Illinois burial-records rescue announced
timeline.description: Comptroller + Bronzeville Historical Society: 140,000+ burial records from shuttered Black-owned funeral homes, transferred to the Harsh Collection.

timeline.title: Mellon $3.5M for Stony Island Archives Innovation Program
timeline.description: Rebuild Foundation grant builds archival infrastructure for the Arts Bank collections.

timeline.title: Twitter/X research API paywall
timeline.description: Spring 2023 restriction breaks the dominant digital-memory research infrastructure.

timeline.title: HBCU Radio Preservation Project $5M grant
timeline.description: Mellon grant to WYSO with NEDCC to preserve 29 HBCU radio stations' archives.

timeline.title: Emmett Till and Mamie Till-Mobley National Monument established
timeline.description: Presidential proclamation; Roberts Temple among the sites.

timeline.title: Mellon $2M Harsh digitization grant
timeline.description: Ends the Harsh Collection's in-person-only era.

timeline.title: MTV News archive wipe
timeline.description: Viacom/Paramount takes the MTV News archive offline.

timeline.title: King and King funeral-home records recovered
timeline.description: Indiana Landmarks' Black Heritage Preservation Program recovers the records before demolition; deposited at Indiana Historical Society.

timeline.title: Knoxville College building fire
timeline.description: Fire destroys a historic building on the closed HBCU campus; records custody undocumented.

timeline.title: Separate Cinema Archive acquired by Lucas Museum
timeline.description: 37,000-item private collection enters a national museum's permanent collection.

timeline.title: John Simmons garage fire
timeline.description: Fire/water damage destroys most of John Simmons's negatives during a move; partial salvage ongoing.

timeline.title: Quintard Taylor dies
timeline.description: Founder of BlackPast.org dies - key-person risk for a major ungated Black-history reference site.

timeline.title: Fisk Rosenwald Fund Archive portal launches
timeline.description: Amistad/John Hope Franklin Research Center portal: ~30,000 documents.

timeline.title: Internet Archive releases BET rescue explorer
timeline.description: Pilot explorer for 199,000+ preserved BET.com articles.

timeline.title: Shorefront reporting (NPR Illinois)
timeline.description: Shorefront Legacy Center's role in Evanston's cash reparations reported; Trump administration suing to end reparations.

timeline.title: Mellon $2M Moorland-Spingarn grant
timeline.description: Five positions, processing, conservation-lab plan, AV digitization at MSRC.

timeline.title: BET.com digital article wipe
timeline.description: BET Digital permanently removes its entire written news archive as a "video-first pivot."
